fields.meta_title: Landing Page SEO: Build One Page per Query | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Landing page SEO in seven steps, with launch checks from Google's own tools and a builder that hands you the page as code. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Landing Page SEO Into Code You Own, Tag by Tag
fields.hero_description: Describe the offer and the query it should answer. Emergent builds the page and its lead form as code you own, with the title tag and schema you specify.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into an SEO Landing Page
fields.features_subheading: The parts of landing page SEO Emergent writes into the page from your prompt, and where its leads are saved.
fields.feature_1:
Meta tags written around the query

Your prompt names the query, and Emergent writes the page's title and description tags around it. Rewording either one later takes a follow-up message that edits the code.
fields.feature_2:
Sections in the order searchers need them

Emergent lays out the H2s around the questions your buyers ask next, in the order you list them. Ask for a pricing or comparison section in the prompt and it gets its own H2.
fields.feature_3:
Structured data and canonical tags

Structured data goes in as JSON-LD, the format Google recommends, for whichever schema.org type your prompt names. A canonical URL and a sitemap entry go in on request too.
fields.feature_4:
Speed findings you can fix by prompt

PageSpeed Insights reports Core Web Vitals for the published page. Paste a finding, such as an image served larger than it displays, into the chat and Emergent fixes the code.
fields.feature_5:
Leads saved with their landing URL

Leads land in a database you own, with the UTM parameters the form records. Add utm_medium=cpc to your ad links, then filter on utm_medium to separate paid leads from the rest.
fields.feature_6:
Markup you can audit and keep

Export the page, form included, to your GitHub repository as plain code. Your developer can then check every tag, JSON-LD included, with whichever crawler they already use.

fields.usecase_heading: SEO Landing Pages for Four Kinds of Query
fields.tab_content_1:
One feature page for one buying query

Northwind sells shift scheduling software, and that phrase is what its buyers search. The prompt puts it in the title tag, H1 and URL, with SoftwareApplication markup for the product. Demo requests land in a table with the landing URL attached.
fields.tab_content_2:
Four branches with copy of their own

A moving company has crews in four Colorado cities, and they do different work. Downtown high-rises lead the Denver page; Boulder's is about student moves. LocalBusiness markup on every page carries the branch address. Quote requests post to the Slack channel of the branch they came from.
fields.tab_content_3:
What a fair comparison table shows

A rival's strengths stay in the table. The Acme vs Globex page keeps the mobile app row, where Globex is ahead. BreadcrumbList markup places the page under Compare, and the feature pages it mentions are linked from the bottom.
fields.tab_content_4:
The template preview comes before the email field

Nothing is gated until the visitor has seen the content calendar template: a preview of the sheet and short notes on filling it in. Maya at Lumen enters her work email and the file downloads. Her new HubSpot contact lists this page as the source.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an SEO Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Give each page one query, and judge the page by the leads it brings in, not by traffic alone.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Match what the top results deliver
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Answer before you ask for anything
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose the single query the page should rank for and check that the top results are pages like yours. If the first page of Google is all guides, write a guide-shaped page or pick another query.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open the top ten and note what they have in common: format, length, whether they show prices, which questions their H2s cover. Match the format, then answer what they skip, such as setup time when every result stops at features.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write a concise title tag that names the query and differs from every other title on the site. The meta description should summarize this page alone, though Google may show text from the page instead.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Answer the query in the opening section, in plain words, and place the form after that answer. Ask only for the fields you will use, and say what happens after someone submits.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Mark up the page with the schema.org type that matches it, and include every property Google lists as required for that type. Then link to the new page from related pages, with anchor text that names its topic.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test the page on a phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Load the page on a mid-range phone before launch. Give every image a width and height attribute and the layout holds still while it loads. Any script in the head that the first screen does not need should carry async or defer.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the page on your own domain. Once a week, set its clicks from search beside the leads in your database. When clicks rise and leads do not, test the offer and the form before rewriting the copy for search.

scope.evidence: H1 "Build Landing Page SEO Into Code You Own, Tag by Tag", meta title "Landing Page SEO: Build One Page per Query | Emergent" and hero "Describe the offer and the query it should answer" cover organic landing pages as a whole, not a PPC or campaign sibling.

intent.evidence: The SERP is how-to guides (Semrush, Unbounce, Instapage) plus an AI Overview: FAQ 1 defines the term, the 7-step how-to is SEO-specific (query choice, title tags, schema required properties, width/height, async/defer), both on-topic PAA questions are answered, the off-topic PAA are skipped, and the meta's promises (seven steps, launch checks from Google's tools, code) are delivered.

specificity.evidence: seo variant in the table ("Prompt for the page and its on-page SEO", "Full control of the code: meta tags, schema, and sitemap"); the vocabulary is SEO's own: "SoftwareApplication markup", "BreadcrumbList markup places the page under Compare", "utm_medium=cpc".

openers.evidence: Body paragraphs open on full sentences: "Your prompt names the query", "Northwind sells shift scheduling software", "A rival's strengths stay in the table", "Choose the single query the page should rank for".

craft.evidence: QC Q2/Q5/Q7 clean. Repeated idea fixed by reviewer: FAQ 3 ended "Emergent builds the page as code you can export to your GitHub repository", which restated why_description's contrast and feature_6 and did not answer the Wix question. The sentence is removed (QC is still TOTAL 0).

voice.evidence: Product-led and concrete: "Downtown high-rises lead the Denver page; Boulder's is about student moves", "Paste a finding, such as an image served larger than it displays, into the chat", "When clicks rise and leads do not, test the offer and the form before rewriting the copy for search".

truth.evidence: UTM fix verified: feature_5 "Add utm_medium=cpc to your ad links, then filter on utm_medium to split paid leads from organic ones" replaces the referrer claim and is sourced to GA4 channel rules; no other field repeats the referrer claim. FAQ 4 now keeps to Google's canonicalization doc ("They can, when each page carries content of its own. When pages are near duplicates, Google picks one as canonical"). The doorway abuse, JSON-LD, A/B canonical, mobile-first, alt text, Wix SEO panel and Landingi types claims are each sourced. All claims_used ids are approved; canonical and sitemap are "on request" (row 14).

distinct.evidence: Paid-only pages go to the PPC landing page (FAQ 4), single storefronts to the local business landing page (FAQ 7), and noindex pages to the thank you page (FAQ 9). The tab segments (feature, city, comparison, template pages) are query types, not channels.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic items (2 PAA, related searches, secondaries), each answered first ("Yes, as an outline, not a design", "They can, when each page carries content of its own"); hub link in item 2; 3 exact-match sibling links.

images.evidence: Each tab matches its copy: uc-1 "Query in the title tag / H1 / URL" and "Demo request saved, Landing URL attached"; uc-2 four cities with their own H1s and #aurora-branch quote; uc-3 Globex ahead on "iOS and Android" with BreadcrumbList Home > Compare > Acme vs Globex; uc-4 preview before the email field and "Contact created in HubSpot". defects: [truth | HUB_RULES 8] feature_5: Escalated from reviewer-batch-m1's note because it is untrue, not merely imprecise. Organic search clicks carry no UTM tags, so filtering a form's UTM field separates tagged paid leads from every untagged lead: direct, referral, email and organic together. The cited source (support.google.com/analytics/answer/10917952) gives utm_medium naming advice ('one unique utm_medium for each distinct channel'). It does not say UTM tags identify organic visits; GA4 does that from the referrer, which this form does not record. The title 'Leads saved with their landing URL' also no longer matches the body. -> "...then filter on utm_medium to separate paid leads from the rest." Or record the referrer as well and say leads referred by a search engine are organic. Bring the title and body back to the same point.

[truth | HUB_RULES 8] faq item 5: Escalated from the reviewer-c5-seo and reviewer-batch-m1 note. The page's own how-to makes launch the same as publishing: step 6 says 'before launch' and step 7 says 'Publish the page on your own domain'. URL Inspection only inspects a URL that Google can fetch on a verified property, so it cannot tell you before launch whether the page can be indexed. As written, this is untrue. -> Make URL Inspection the first check after publishing ("After publishing, run URL Inspection..."), and keep the Rich Results Test and canonical check before launch.
